subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should OpenClaw add a narrow binary-document fallback to the read tool now, or defer this behavior to broader document parsing/provider-native file work?
rationale: Current source still has the token-waste behavior, but the permanent boundary affects core tool UX, PDF-tool routing, Office parser security, and overlapping document capability issues.

options.title: Land bounded fallback
options.body: Add a current-main read guard for known PDF/Office container formats with bounded detection, clear fallback text, and tests that preserve normal text and image reads.

options.title: Fold into document architecture
options.body: Keep read unchanged for now and track the behavior through the broader document extraction and provider-native file issues after maintainer design approval.

recommendation.title: Land bounded fallback
recommendation.body: Add a current-main read guard for known PDF/Office container formats with bounded detection, clear fallback text, and tests that preserve normal text and image reads.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main ownership signal is on the read-wrapper and session read-tool boundary where the narrow fallback would live.
